battle.name: 始州之戰
battle.brief: 北周大象二年九月，益州人李嚴聚眾為亂、據成都，勢蔓延梁益二州。朝廷命隨國公楊堅率兵入蜀討之，由漢中出劍門，於利州始州一線遇敵。始州控蜀北門戶，叛軍據城拒守，官軍以弩箭壓住城頭，再以步騎出關反擊，潰其主力，李嚴西走。亞述長弓的弓兵開路、車兵隨進用法，在此改由弩手與角弓分擔。

kit.name: 亞述長弓
kit.history: 亞述人靠弓和鐵的組合征服兩河流域。弓兵在車上射，車兵靠弓兵開路。

countries: 北周一方是中原王朝的中央政權。大象二年七月周宣帝宇文邕病逝，皇太子宇文闡即位，是為靜帝，年方六歲，國政由大丞相楊堅與數名重臣共掌，遂令隨國公楊堅以行軍總管的身分率禁軍宿衛與關中、漢中、劍州一線的邊軍入蜀。後方是長安經劍閣道至劍州、益州的水陸糧道，前線則是利州總管府所屬的始州等四郡六縣。叛方不是外國，而是北周邊內的地方起事：起事首領李嚴是益州本地人，裹挾了州縣吏員、地方豪右以及巴蜀山地中的僚、羌諸部眾，據成都立寨，並向梁州伸展，企圖在蜀北門戶的始州一線設防，把官軍擋在劍門關外。整場衝突沒有第三國正式參與，陳朝隔著長江只能遙為聲援，是否曾遣使接通，諸說並存。北周的目標是收回益梁二州、恢復朝廷對蜀地的直接控制與賦稅；叛軍的目標則是據蜀自立、割據一方，把水陸要道握在手中。格局上，北周滅齊之後正當對陳用兵失利，蜀地恰好成了中原與江南拉鋸的後方，誰控制劍閣道，誰就握住了西南的底牌。
countriesEn: The Zhou side was the Central Plains dynasty itself. In the seventh month of the Daxiang era Emperor Xuan of Zhou, Yuwen Yong, died of illness; his heir Yuwen Chan, aged six, ascended the throne as Emperor Jing, and state power passed into the hands of the chancellor Yang Jian and a handful of senior ministers. Yang Jian, Duke of Sui, was accordingly entrusted with the title of commander-in-chief and led the imperial guard, the household troops and the frontier garrison drawn from Guanzhong, Hanzhong and the Jianzhou area into Shu. Behind him lay the grain route running from Chang'an along the Jianmen plank road to Jianzhou and Yizhou by water and road alike; in front lay Shizhou and the four commanderies and six counties of the Lizhou governorship. The insurgents were not a foreign power but a local rising inside Zhou's own borders. Their leader, Li Yan, was a native of Yizhou, and he drew in commandery officials, local magnates, and the Liao, Qiang and other groups of the Sichuan mountains; they made Chengdu their base, reached east into Liangzhou, and dug in along Shizhou, the northern gateway of Shu, hoping to hold the imperial army outside the Jianmen Pass. No third state took part officially, and the Chen court across the Yangtze could only offer distant sympathy; whether envoys ever passed between the two is a matter of dispute. Zhou's aim was to recover Yi and Liang, restore direct imperial control over Shu and resume its tax revenue; the insurgents' aim was to establish an independent regime in Shu and hold the water and land routes in their own hands. In the wider picture, Zhou had just destroyed Northern Qi and was having no success against Chen, and Shu had become the rear of the Central Plains; whoever held the Jianmen road held the strategic card in the southwest.
people: 決定這場戰役走向的是三個人。第一個是隨國公楊堅：宣帝既崩、靜帝幼弱的亂局中，他手上握著北周實際的兵柄，這次平蜀是他第一次以主帥身分獨當一面。他的用兵取向很清楚——蜀道艱狹，劍閣棧道容不下大隊人馬，於是以輕裝前鋒先出關，主力與糧秣沿河谷推進，不在深山裡與叛軍拼消耗；及至援軍抵達始州城下，也不急著強攻，而是先封住叛軍退路與糧道，再以步騎出關反擊，把攻城器械與部眾一起擠離城牆。戰後他沒有對蜀地作大規模懲罰，歸附的州縣官吏多照舊留任，賦役獲得寬減，蜀地因此很快安靜下來。這份不專恃力、講求速勝的作風，讓關中與河北的朝野更認定他既有將才亦有柄力。第二個是益州起事首領李嚴：他以成都為根本，東聯梁州，北據始州與四郡六縣的城寨，敗後西走，餘眾散入山地，其生平與終局在諸史中只留數語，諸說並存。第三個是靜帝宇文闡本人：六歲登基、不能視事，全部決策都落在重臣手裡，他雖未出現在戰場上，卻是這場戰役得以由北周一方發動的政治前提；同年十一月益州刺史王謙再舉兵亂，也可見蜀地局勢並非一次用兵所能定。
peopleEn: Three men shaped the outcome. The first was Yang Jian, Duke of Sui: with Xuan dead and Jing a child, real military power in the Zhou rested in his hands, and the pacification of Shu was the first time he commanded a campaign in his own right. His approach was plain. The roads of Shu are narrow and the Jianmen plank road cannot hold a mass of men, so he sent lightly equipped columns out of the pass first while the main body and the baggage trains moved up the river valleys, refusing to exhaust his troops in a duel of attrition among the mountains. When the relieving force reached the walls of Shizhou he did not rush the assault: he sealed the insurgents' line of retreat and their supply route first, then counterattacked with foot and horse out of the pass, tearing the siege engines and the ranks away from the wall. Afterwards he did not reshape Shu by punitive decree; officials who submitted were mostly left in post and the corvée was reduced, which is why the region settled so quickly. That mixture of speed and unwillingness to rely on force alone convinced the court and the Hebei gentry alike that he had both generalship and weight of command. The second was Li Yan, the Yizhou rebel leader: he based himself on Chengdu, reached east to Liangzhou, held Shizhou and the forts of the four commanderies and six counties in the north, and after his defeat fled west, his followers scattering into the mountains; his life and his end survive only in a few words, and the accounts differ. The third was Emperor Jing, Yuwen Chan himself. He was six years old and could not govern, and every decision lay with the ministers; he never appeared on the battlefield, yet his accession was the political premise that allowed the campaign to be launched at all. The renewed rising of Wang Qian, governor of Yizhou, in the eleventh month of the same year shows that the situation in Shu was not settled by a single campaign.
kits: 本卡的主兵器是亞述長弓，即兩河流域的角木複合弓：弓背以木為胎，兩端包角，貼附筋腱，張力遠勝單純木弓，亞述人正是靠弓與鐵的組合在車上展開射擊，車兵則跟在弓兵打開的缺口前進。需要說明的是，亞述帝國在前七世紀末便已覆滅，這件兵器本身不會出現在公元五八零年的蜀中山地；它代表的是複合弓一系的技術譜系——角、木、筋的形制經西亞、中亞傳入草原，匈奴、嚈噠、突厥以至北周邊軍所用的角弓，正是這條線的末端，在隋唐仍為騎兵標配。真正決定始州攻防的遠射武器是弩：蹶張弩以腳踏或二人合力張弦，臨陣射速可數倍於拉弓；桃園弩張力更大，可洞穿甲葉，專用於攻城與破壞守軍的器械。除弓弩之外，兩軍尚有步槍、長矛、刀、戟，配札甲與鍪、牌，帶弓、矢囊、投石索；攻城一方有雲梯、撞車、投石機與擲石之具，守城一方有城堞、擂石、滾木、拒馬、鹿角。蜀地馬匹有限，步卒為主、騎兵為輔；糧秣靠嘉陵江、沱江水運與劍閣棧道人力挑擔相接。
kitsEn: The card's principal weapon is the Assyrian bow, the horn-and-wood composite bow of Mesopotamia: a wooden core, horn at the tips, sinew backing, far more powerful than a plain wooden bow. It was the combination of bow and iron that let the Assyrians shoot from their chariots, with the chariotry following behind the gaps the archers opened. It should be said plainly that Assyria itself fell before the end of the seventh century BC, and this weapon cannot have been present in the mountains of Shu in AD 580. What it represents is a technical lineage: the horn, wood and sinew composite travelled from West Asia through Central Asia onto the steppe, and the recurved horn bows used by the Xiongnu, the Hephthalites, the Turks and by Zhou's own frontier troops were the far end of that line, remaining standard kit for cavalry under the Sui and Tang. The long-range weapons that actually decided the fighting at Shizhou were crossbows: the traction crossbow was strung by a team of two or by foot pressure, giving a rate of fire several times that of the bow, while the much stronger Taoyuan crossbow could pierce armour and was used against walls and engines. Beside bows and crossbows both armies carried spears, lances, sabres, halberds, lamellar armour, helmets and shields, together with bow cases, quivers and slings. The besiegers brought scaling ladders, battering rams, traction trebuchets and stone-throwing bolts, while the defenders answered with parapets, rolling logs, stones dropped from the walls, cheval-de-frise and spiked barriers. Horses were scarce in Shu, so the armies fought mainly on foot with cavalry in support; grain moved by boat on the Jialing and Tuo rivers and was carried on the plank road on men's backs.
tactics: 這場戰役的樣貌，是由蜀北的地形決定的。始州治所在劍閣，控著劍門關的南口，關道依山而築，寬不過數步，大隊人馬與攻城器具在此根本展不開；山脊上的城寨居高臨下，可以俯瞰河谷，官軍的車兵、雲梯一旦進入谷口就暴露在守軍的矢石之下。因此楊堅不把主力押在棧道上：前鋒以輕裝徒步隊伍先出關，佔領關南要道與渡口，步軍主力沿白龍江與嘉陵江河谷分批推進，糧船與輜重走水路，棧道只用來輸送輕兵與挑夫，形成山道、水道兩條並行的縱隊，而不是一個可以展開的方陣。攻始州時，弩手先在城外列陣，以齊射覆蓋城頭與城郊的射孔，逼守軍縮回堞後；投石機與撞車隨後才進抵門下，步卒再以雲梯攀城，試圖在守軍弩火間隙中登頂。叛軍真正的弱點不在城牆，而在水與糧：援軍抵達後，官軍並不急著強攻，而是先以騎兵切斷叛軍往梁州與成都的退路、以輕兵封住上游糧道，再以步騎出關作正面反擊，攻城器械失去掩護，部眾被擠離城牆，潰散於山地。追擊不宜深入叢林，故官軍隨即改為據險設屯、斷其糧水、分路招撫，叛軍首腦西走，餘眾星散，收束以安撫為主。
tacticsEn: The shape of this battle was decided by the terrain in the north of Shu. Shizhou was sited at Jiange, controlling the southern mouth of the Jianmen Pass, a road cut along the mountain no more than a few paces wide; a formed army and its siege engines could not deploy there at all, and the forts on the ridge above the valley could look down on the approach, so the attackers' chariots and ladders were exposed to arrows and stones as soon as they entered the defile. Yang Jian therefore refused to put his main force on the plank road. Light columns went out of the pass first to hold the defiles and crossings south of it; the infantry pushed up in batches along the valleys of the Bailong and the Jialing; grain boats and baggage moved by water, and the plank road carried only light troops and porters, so the army advanced as two parallel columns instead of a deployable line. Against Shizhou, crossbowmen first formed up outside the walls and covered the parapets and the shooting slits of the suburb with volleys, driving the defenders back behind the crenellations; only then did the traction trebuchets and the rams come up to the gates, and infantry attempted the walls on ladders, trying to reach the top in the gaps between the bolts. The insurgents' real weakness was not the wall but water and grain. When the relieving force arrived, the attackers did not press the siege: cavalry cut the road back to Liangzhou and Chengdu, light troops sealed the supply route upstream, and then foot and horse came out of the pass to counterattack. With the siege engines left without cover, the ranks were pushed off the wall and scattered into the hills. Pursuit into the thickets was useless, so the field army set fortified camps on the heights, cut the insurgents' water and grain, and moved to recover and pacify; the rebel leader fled west, the rest dissolved, and the closing phase was mostly a matter of amnesty.
data: 可以核實的數字有限，先列可用的部分。始州是西魏廢帝三年554年改安州所置，治所在今四川省劍閣縣，東經約一百零五點六度、北緯約三十二點三度，領四郡——普安、黃原、安都、潼川，六縣——普安、水歸、胡原、黃安、茂陵、武連；北周時屬利州總管府，隋大業三年改稱普安郡，唐武德元年復稱始州，先天二年改名劍州，這一組地名可互相對照，說明此地正是蜀道北口的鎖鑰。距離上，劍門關至始州的谷道約二十至三十里，步行一日可達；始州順沱江、嘉陵江河谷南下至成都約三百至四百公里；劍門關至長安的棧道行程則在千公里以上，糧秣全賴水運轉接。兵員方面，正史沒有留下編制數字，只以概略的說法帶過：李嚴起事眾至數萬，北周方面出動的是行軍總管直轄的宿衛與關中、漢中、劍州邊軍組成的混成部隊，規模同樣無法復原。裝備數據中較可靠的一項是弩：漢代弩機張力在百公斤一級，蹶張弩需雙人合力或以腳蹶，桃園弩張力更大，可洞穿甲葉；射速則數倍於拉弓。時間上，起事繫於大象二年九月，蜀地平定歷時數月，諸史只用概略字眼帶過，並無逐日記載；而同年十一月益州刺史王謙再反，說明第一次平定並未徹底解決地方問題。
dataEn: The verifiable figures are few, and those available come first. Shizhou was created in the third year of the Xixiao reign of Western Wei, 554, when Anzhou was renamed; it was administered at present-day Jiange County in Sichuan, at roughly 105.6 degrees east and 32.3 degrees north, and comprised four commanderies - Puan, Huangyuan, Andu and Tongchuan - and six counties - Puan, Shuigui, Huyuan, Huang'an, Maoling and Wulian. Under Northern Zhou it belonged to the Lizhou governorship; in the third year of the Daye era of Sui it was renamed Puan Commandery, restored to Shizhou in the first year of Wude by the Tang, and renamed Jianzhou in the second year of Xiantian. That chain of names fixes the place exactly: it is the lock and key of the northern mouth of the Shu roads. As for distances, the valley road from the Jianmen Pass to Shizhou runs twenty to thirty li, a single day's walk; from Shizhou down the Tuo and Jialing valleys to Chengdu is some three hundred to four hundred kilometres; and from the Jianmen Pass to Chang'an the plank road journey exceeds a thousand kilometres, so all grain had to be transferred to water transport. On strength, no official figures survive in the histories, which speak only in general terms: Li Yan's rising swelled to tens of thousands, and Zhou's force was a mixed body of imperial guard and frontier troops from Guanzhong, Hanzhong and Jianzhou under the commander-in-chief, whose size cannot be reconstructed. The most reliable equipment figure concerns the crossbow: Han-era locks developed about a hundred kilogrammes of pull, the traction crossbow needed two men or a foot pedal to cock, and the Taoyuan crossbow, still stronger, could pierce armour; its rate of fire was several times that of the bow. On timing, the rising is placed in the ninth month of the Daxiang second year, and the pacification took a number of months, the histories using only general words and keeping no day-by-day record; the renewed revolt of Wang Qian, governor of Yizhou, in the eleventh month of the same year shows that the first suppression had not settled the question.
cause: 起事的前提，是北周對蜀地的治理一直存在裂縫。蜀中自十六國以來歷經前蜀、後蜀等割據政權，州郡豪右與中央的關係一向微妙；北周接管巴蜀之後，益州的賦役、徵發與兵源調度仍多倚賴地方勢力，朝廷派出的刺史與邊軍彼此牽制，一遇災荒或上命過苛，怨氣便會匯聚到一點。外部環境同樣重要：北周的主力自大象元年起接連伐陳而多不得志，而蜀地正是中原南向的後方與補給線，宣帝甚至有經蜀道向江南輸兵輸糧的打算；此時蜀中一亂，江南便可利用蜀道把兵員與物資送到關中背後，這是朝廷不能容忍的。直接導火線是大象二年九月，益州人李嚴聚眾為亂：起事很快占據成都，梁州數郡響應，叛軍北上，在蜀北門戶的始州一線設寨布防，試圖把官軍擋在劍門關外，以為割據之資。至於起事的口號、組織章程，李嚴的出身與年歲，以及叛軍是否曾與陳朝通使求援，現存記載皆無明文，諸說並存。可以確定的是：蜀地長期積累的治理矛盾，遇上北周對外用兵、內部多事的一個空檔，造就了這場叛亂；而同年接連發生的帝室與地方叛亂，說明北周末年的權力真空已深。
causeEn: The premise of the rising was that Zhou's rule in Shu had always been cracked. Since the Sixteen Kingdoms the region had passed through regimes such as Former Shu and Later Shu, and the relationship between the commandery magnates and the central government had always been delicate. After Zhou took over Bashu, the taxes, the levies and the recruitment of troops in Yizhou still leaned on local power, with the court's own governors and the frontier garrison pulling against each other, and whenever famine or an over-severe order came down, the resentment gathered to a point. The external situation mattered just as much. Zhou's main army had been campaigning against Chen without success since the first year of Daxiang, and Shu was the rear and the supply line of the Central Plains; the emperor had even toyed with sending men and grain south by way of the Shu roads, and if Shu rose, the south could use those roads to bring troops and supplies around behind Guanzhong, which the court could not tolerate. The immediate spark was the ninth month of the Daxiang second year, when Li Yan, a native of Yizhou, gathered a crowd and rose. The movement took Chengdu quickly, several commanderies of Liangzhou answered, and the rebels pushed north to fortify the line of Shizhou at the northern gateway of Shu, hoping to hold the imperial army outside the Jianmen Pass and make a base for separatism. The slogans, the organisation and the constitution of the rising, Li Yan's origins and age, and whether the rebels ever sent envoys to the Chen court for help are all without clear record; the accounts differ. What can be established is this: the accumulated grievances of a long-unquiet region met the moment when Zhou was exhausted by war abroad and beset by disorder within, and that combination produced the rising; and the succession of revolts at the court and in the provinces in the same year shows how deep the power vacuum at the end of Zhou had become.
impact: 此役的後果分成兩層。眼前一層是蜀地的平定：始州及四郡六縣的城寨重歸朝廷直接控制，叛軍首腦西走，餘眾散入山地，益梁二州的城池與編戶重新歸入版籍，北周在西南的兵源與糧源從此可以就近徵發，不必再仰賴關中的長途運補；但同年十一月益州刺史王謙再度舉兵，說明地方權力結構的問題並未因一次用兵而消解。深一層的影響落在楊堅身上：始州之戰是他以行軍總管身分第一次獨當一面、迅速平定西南邊亂的功績，朝野由此更認定他既有將才亦有柄力；同年他又平定了尉遲迥在黎陽的兵變，開皇元年進而代周建隋。對南面的陳朝而言，蜀地歸北周等於失去一條向西北伸出的臂膀，蜀道南北兩端都握在隋的手中，日後隋軍東下滅陳、經略吐谷渾與劍南，都以此為基地。技術層面上，弩在西南山地攻防中的地位再次被確認：守城以弩壓制谷口、行軍以弩手掩護縱隊前進的作法，後來在兵書中成為西南常規；劍閣棧道對大軍補給的制約也再度顯現，蜀道自此被視為只能單向深入的窄門。
impactEn: The consequences work on two levels. On the near level, Shu was pacified: Shizhou and the forts of the four commanderies and six counties returned to the direct control of the court, the rebel leader fled west, the remainder scattered into the mountains, and the cities and registered households of Yi and Liang were entered again in the imperial registers, so that Zhou could now draw its soldiers and grain in the southwest from close at hand instead of carrying them by long haul from Guanzhong. Yet the renewed revolt of Wang Qian, governor of Yizhou, in the eleventh month of the same year shows that the structure of local power was not resolved by a single campaign. On the deeper level the effect fell on Yang Jian. Shizhou was the first time he had commanded an independent operation as commander-in-chief and had crushed a revolt in the southwest with speed, and the court and the Hebei gentry drew from it the conclusion that he had both generalship and weight of command; in the same year he put down Yuchi Jiong's revolt at Liyang, and in the Kaihuang first year he went on to replace Zhou with the Sui. For the Chen court in the south, Shu in Zhou's hands meant the loss of an arm reaching north-west; both ends of the Shu road were now in the hands of the Sui, and the later Sui campaigns against Chen, against the Tuyuhun and in southern Sichuan all drew on that base. On the technical level the crossbow's standing in mountain attack and defence in the southwest was confirmed once more: crossbowmen holding the passes while the column advanced under their cover became a regular practice in the southern theatre, recorded in the military manuals. The Jianmen plank road's constraint on supply was visible again, and the Shu road came to be treated as a door that can be entered but not easily left.
result: 打到最後，始州城下的叛軍主力被壓垮：攻城器械在弩火覆蓋下失去作用，部眾退散，首領李嚴西走，餘眾或散入山林，益梁二州的城池與編戶重新歸入朝廷版籍。朝廷沒有對蜀地作大規模的懲罰性改造，歸附的州縣官吏多照舊留任，賦役獲得寬減，因此表面的平定很快轉成實質的歸附，這在史家的評價中常被視為楊堅用兵不專恃力的一面。殘餘叛眾在山區零星抵抗，斷續數月，直到地方軍鎮完成清剿與改置州縣才算收束；同年十一月的王謙之亂，又把蜀地拖入另一輪動盪。整體而言，北周用一次規模不大而時機恰當的用兵，保住了西南邊防，也讓楊堅在通往皇位的路上再行一步。至於此役的俘獲數、耗糧數與行軍日程，正史皆未記載，只有《隋書》《北史》數語概括為蜀平；連同起事經過、李嚴下落等細節，學界至今多作保留，諸說並存。
resultEn: In the end the main body of the insurgents was crushed before Shizhou: the siege engines lost all effect under the crossbow fire, the ranks dispersed, Li Yan fled west, and the survivors either scattered into the hills; the cities and registered households of Yi and Liang returned to the imperial registers. The court did not reshape Shu by punitive decree; submitted commandery and county officials were mostly left in post and the corvée was reduced, so a surface pacification quickly became a real submission, and historians have often read this as the mark of a commander who did not rely on force alone. The remnants resisted fitfully in the mountains for a number of months, until the local garrisons completed the reduction and the redistribution of commanderies and counties; then the rising of Wang Qian in the eleventh month of the same year dragged Shu into another round of unrest. On the whole, Zhou preserved its southwestern frontier with one small and well-timed stroke of force, and Yang Jian took one more step towards the throne. As for the tally of captures, the grain consumed and the marching schedule, the official histories record none; only a few words in the History of Sui and the History of the Northern Dynasties sum it up as the pacification of Shu. The course of the rising, the fate of Li Yan and many other details remain matters of reserve for scholars, and the accounts differ.
